media.altText: Detail of a 1933 press photograph showing Marcella Halicz in profile, wearing a pearl necklace.
media.description: Identification follows the archival caption, which names the guests: Jan Kiepura fifth from the right, the Paris photographer Zygmunt Frenkiel first from the left, Bronisław Kaper second from the left, the director Ryszard Ordyński fifth from the left, the singer Adam Didur ninth from the right, the poet Jan Lechoń in the centre in spectacles, Kaper's wife in the centre, and — among the women at the right edge — Kiepura's secretary Marcella Halicz together with Alicja Brun, whom the caption distinguishes as the one holding a photograph of Kiepura. The woman shown in this detail stands beside the guest holding that photograph and is therefore Halicz. The detail was located in the full frame by correlation: it corresponds to a 315 × 466 px region of the 2035 × 2560 px scan and is reproduced here enlarged.
media.publicCaption: Marcella Halicz, Jan Kiepura's secretary and the author of the Polish lyrics of Ninon, ach uśmiechnij się! and Signorina, signorina, at the cocktail reception Kiepura gave in Paris in November 1933. Detail of the group photograph in which Kaper stands second from the left.
media.publicCreditLine: Narodowe Archiwum Cyfrowe, Koncern Ilustrowany Kurier Codzienny – Archiwum Ilustracji, ref. 3/1/0/11/8270/3; the frame was published in Światowid 46 (483), 11 November 1933.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The National Digital Archive records the object as public domain and states that it may be reproduced, adapted and distributed, including commercially, without permission. The archive holds an enlarged detail (420 × 622 px) cropped from the 2035 × 2560 px scan of the full group photograph, which is registered separately.
media.title: Marcella Halicz — detail of the reception for Jan Kiepura, Paris, November 1933

timelineEvents.title: Marriage
timelineEvents.label: 30 June 1927 · Marriage in Berlin
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper marries Eleonora Sirot in Berlin.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Kaper marries Eleonora de domo Sirot in Berlin on June 30.

timelineEvents.title: Arrival in New York en route to Los Angeles
timelineEvents.label: 24 Oct 1934 · Arrival in New York
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper arrives in New York from France with Eleonora, holding a temporary visa and travelling onward to Los Angeles.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Kaper and his wife Eleonora arrived in New York aboard the S.S. Champlain from Le Havre on 24 October 1934, with Los Angeles listed as their destination.

timelineEvents.title: Legal Permanent Entry
timelineEvents.label: 1 Nov 1935 · Permanent U.S. entry
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper enters the United States for permanent residence through Calexico with Eleonora.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Enters for permanent residence at Calexico, California, from Mexicali on 1 November 1935, travelling on foot with Eleonora. The manifest records 6626 Franklin Ave., Hollywood, as his U.S. destination; his Declaration of Intention four months later records the same address as his residence.

timelineEvents.title: Declarations of Intention
timelineEvents.label: 4 Feb 1936 · Declarations of Intention
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Bronisław and Eleonora Kaper file Declarations of Intention to become U.S. citizens in Los Angeles.
timelineEvents.longDescription: On 4 February 1936, Bronisław Kaper and Eleonora Kaper each filed a Declaration of Intention in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California, Los Angeles. Bronisław Kaper’s declaration records him as residing at Château des Fleurs, 6626 Franklin Ave., Hollywood.
